text: Seabrook Town beat Harbour City 4-2 in the Northbridge League, overturning a two-goal deficit after the break. Harbour City started strong, scoring twice just before and after halftime thanks to Elias Okafor and Marek Barros, who was the standout player with 1 goal, 2 assists, and 9 interceptions [#905] [#975] [#975]. Despite scoring early, Harbour City couldn't match Seabrook’s dominance in the second half, as Seabrook’s 3-4-3 setup pushed harder with more direct play and aggressive pressing from the 65th minute [#1361]. This tactic sparked four goals, including a late brace by Kian Romano who scored two quick goals in injury time to seal the comeback [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook created the better chances, taking 22 shots to Harbour City's 10 and controlling more possession (53.4% compared to 46.6%). The match was a thrilling example of how quick counterattacks and wide crosses paid off for Seabrook, while Harbour City’s patient, short-passing style fell short in the end.

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with xG values of 0.27, 0.206, 0.609, and 0.959, overturning a 2-0 deficit to win 4-2 [#1104,#1448,#1882,#1906].
- Harbour City led 2-0 by 47' with goals at 45' (xG 0.111) and 47' (xG 0.009) but failed to capitalize on xG of 1.0 total [#905,#975].
- Seabrook Town increased press intensity and directness from 65', chasing the game and scoring 4 goals in the second half [#1361].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) was man of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, 5 key passes, and a rating of 9.8 despite team loss [#975].
- Harbour City had fewer shots (10 vs 22), shots on target (5 vs 9), and lower possession (46.6% vs 53.4%) than Seabrook Town, indicating Seabrook’s dominance in chance creation [team_stats].

- Seabrook Town’s comeback was fueled by high pressing and increased directness after the 65th minute tactical shift, indicating a switch to more aggressive, direct forward play and a higher defensive line, consistent with chasing the game dynamics [1361]. This reflects their 3-4-3 formation emphasizing wide crossing and forward runs.
- Harbour City’s initial goals came from patient buildup play and precise short passing, leveraging their 4-2-3-1 formation to create through balls, as seen in Elias Okafor’s goal after a 56.7-second 17-pass buildup and Barros’s cross from a corner [904,905,973,975].
- Seabrook’s equalizer and winning goals came from quick regains and counter-attacks, exploiting turnovers with few passes but fast transitions, exemplified by Kian Romano’s late goals following regains and through passes from wide midfielders and forwards [1881,1882,1905,1906].
- The high number of box touches (Seabrook 57 vs. Harbour 42) and more corners (9 vs. 6) for Seabrook highlight their focus on wide crossing and overloads in attacking zones, leveraging their formation’s wingbacks and wide attackers, contrasting with Harbour City’s more cautious, possession-based style [team_stats].
